PLY-01.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:592 ply.merge (tools/soedit/ops/plyops.js merge); tools/gui/ext/models/sub/ply.client.js:161 Join into this mesh
PLY-01.note: Adds another mesh of the model to the picked one, in place or into a new file; an optional matrix places the added mesh. No three file dialogs: both meshes are picked from the model.

PLY-02.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:592 ply.merge, ply.mergeChild (plyops.js merge reconciles the vertex formats)
PLY-02.note: Different vertex layouts are brought to one without a question; what was changed comes back in the result and is shown on the page.

PLY-03.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:604 ply.mergeChild; ply.client.js:164 Join its mesh into the parent
PLY-03.note: Writes <parent>_merged_<child>.ply when the parent has no mesh of its own. Differs from SOEdit: the child bone and its volumes stay; only its mesh view is removed. A child with animation gets a warning that the merged mesh is frozen at rest. Normals are carried over as they are (not renormalised after a scaled bone).

PLY-04.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:624 ply.demerge; ply.client.js:168 Split into child bones
PLY-04.note: SOEdit is broken here (Cancel meant split by connections, bounds left stale). Done right: the split is picked by name (parts, material or loose pieces), each new <base>_demerge_NNN.ply gets its own bounds, optional recentring moves each piece to its own child bone <bone>_part_NNN, and the parent keeps the whole mesh only when asked.

PLY-05.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:666 ply.tweak, mat.set, mat.textures; ply.client.js:179 Apply the flags, part materials section
PLY-05.test: model-edit-ply.test.js: edit/ply skin, tweak; ply.test.js ok 8
PLY-05.note: Mesh flags per part, vertex flags, material names and texture lists per part. Changes stay in the document until Save (one undo step each); no .bak file is needed because nothing is overwritten before Save and a removed file is moved aside, not deleted.

PLY-06.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:781 state ply.get (plyops.js info); ply.client.js:106 facts lines and the parts table
PLY-06.note: Shows bounds, vertex size, vertex flags, layout, blocks in the file, counts, normals, tangents, texture coordinate sets, skin bones, and per part the kind, flags by name, triangles and material. SOEdit printed the FVF as 0x followed by a decimal number; here flags are named.

PLY-07.where: tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:666 ply.tweak (set/clear for mesh flags, vset/vclear for vertex flags); ply.client.js:179
PLY-07.note: SOEdit is broken here: the V radio wrote mesh flag bits into the vertex flags. Done right: mesh flags and vertex flags are separate fields and never mix.

PLY-08.where: tools/lib/model/ply.js write, called by every op through tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js encode()
PLY-08.test: model-edit-ply.test.js: every op test parses each returned file; files no op touches stay byte-identical
PLY-08.note: SOEdit is broken here (an extra 0 byte for an empty texture name, SUBM written as MESH, unknown blocks dropped). Done right: all writes go through the library writer, which keeps SUBM as SUBM, keeps unknown blocks and writes empty names correctly; a mesh no op changed keeps every byte.

PLY-09.note: SUBM, BAS2, SKIN, ADJA, SHDW, IND4 and MROR are read by the library parser.

PLY-X1.where: tools/lib/model/obj.js parse/toMesh; tools/lib/model/edit/ply.js:674 ply.import; tools/gui/ext/models/sub/ply.server.js import-read; ply.client.js:215 Bring in
PLY-X1.test: model-obj.test.js; model-edit-ply.test.js: edit/ply import OBJ, export OBJ round trip; ply.test.js ok 10, ok 12
PLY-X1.note: Addition, not in SOEdit: import OBJ. Units metres (x20) or game units, axis Y up or Z up, polygons made into triangles, normals and tangents made when missing, texture V flipped, winding turned to the game's, one simple .mtl per OBJ material, placed on a bone. The OBJ is read from any folder; only the mod is written, on Save. OBJ has no bone weights, so a skinned mesh cannot come from OBJ: the page says so and points to .ply files, which can be brought in as they are.

PLY-X2.note: Addition, not in SOEdit: export OBJ with a simple OBJ .mtl naming each part's main texture, in metres or game units, Y up or Z up. A skinned mesh exports its rest shape only; the page says the weights are not kept.
